subject: DPA follow-up: onshore backup access, escrow proof & deletion timeline
messages:
From: Alice Lam <alice.lam@auroradata.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@auroradata.com
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on DPA retention & onshore access (Aurora)

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for sending over the draft DPA. Before we proceed to legal review, Aurora has a couple of follow-ups specifically around backup/escrow access and deletion proofing: 

1) Backups & onshore access: we need explicit language confirming that any restoration or support access to backups containing Aurora customer data will occur onshore (US) only, and that access requires a documented internal approval (name + role) from Redwood.

2) Proof of deletion/erasures: procurement needs a mechanism to obtain time-stamped proof that requested erasures were executed (including any on-prem snapshot or tape receipts) within the 30-day window in section 4.2.

3) Escrow and third-party restores: if Redwood uses a third-party backup provider for cold storage, we require a clause describing vendor controls and whether Redwood can unilaterally restore those backups without Aurora consent.

I'm attaching a short list of questions. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a redline requiring: (a) confirmation of onshore-only support restores, (b) an auditable deletion certificate within 30 days, and (c) vendor controls summary?

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Best,
Alice Lam
Contracts Manager, Aurora Data
Attachment: Aurora_DPA_Retention_Questions_20280409.pdf (pdf, 74KB)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Alice Lam <alice.lam@auroradata.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA retention & onshore access (Aurora)

Alice — thanks for the clear list. We're aligned on the desire for stronger evidence and minimizing cross-border access. High level responses below; I'm looping Legal (Naomi) and Product (Karthik) for concrete redline language.

1) Onshore support restores: we can accept an onshore-only restores commitment for customer-triggered restores and Redwood-initiated support restores that contain Aurora customer data. We need to preserve an exception for emergency fraud/malicious-actor investigations where cross-border access may be required; those would require escalation and written notice within 48 hours.

2) Deletion/erasures: we can provide a time-stamped deletion certificate for primary service data and replicated storage we control. Backups and immutable snapshots are typically covered by retention schedules; we can provide a certificate showing when the snapshot record was marked for purge and the purge job execution time. For offline tape/third-party cold storage, we need to confirm process with vendor.

3) Third-party backups: Redwood will supply a vendor controls summary and confirm that we will not restore to Aurora production endpoints without documented Aurora approval, except under the emergency investigatory exception noted above.

I'll circulate proposed redline language by tomorrow EOD. If Aurora prefers a one-hour call to walk through, we can schedule.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Platform Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference, Inc.

From: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Questions on DPA retention & onshore access (Aurora) — proposed redlines

Hi Alice,

Thanks for the note. Attached are three narrow redlines we propose for inclusion in the DPA; they map to your numbered items. Summary below + excerpt language.

A) Onshore Restores: "Redwood shall ensure that any personnel access to Aurora Data customer content for the purpose of restoration or incident response shall be performed from servers and operator terminals physically located within the United States unless (i) Aurora provides prior written consent, or (ii) Redwood reasonably determines in good faith that immediate cross-border access is necessary to investigate an active security incident; Redwood shall provide written notice to Aurora within 48 hours of such access and a post-incident report within 7 days."

B) Deletion Certificate: "Upon Aurora's written request, Redwood will provide a time-stamped deletion certificate summarizing: (i) the identifier of the data subject to deletion, (ii) the systems/locations searched, (iii) the dates/times of deletion jobs executed, (iv) the backup/snapshot identifiers impacted, and (v) the responsible Redwood approver. Certificate generation will be completed within thirty (30) days of a validated deletion request."

C) Third-Party Backups: "Redwood will provide an information security summary for any third-party backup provider that stores Aurora customer content. Redwood shall not initiate restores from such third-party repositories to Aurora production endpoints without Aurora's prior written approval, except in the case of the emergency investigatory exception described above."

We call out one practical limitation: for truly immutable snapshots (e.g., some cloud provider snapshot chains), the deletion action can be the marking of snapshot for purge and the execution of the purge job; we propose the certificate reflect that lifecycle.

I've put the redlines in a doc and attached: Jonas, happy if you want to refine coordination language on the incident exception.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Jonas_response_redlines_20280412.docx (docx, 12KB)

From: Alice Lam <alice.lam@auroradata.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@auroradata.com
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 11:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA retention & onshore access (Aurora) — proposed redlines

Naomi, Jonas — appreciate the fast turnaround and very reasonable language. A few clarifying requests from Aurora legal/procurement: 

• Incident exception: can we broaden the notice window to "no later than 72 hours" and require a short description of the legal/regulatory basis for the cross-border access in the post-incident report?

• Deletion certificate: procurement would prefer the certificate to include the hash/ID for the purge job where available, and to state whether any archived/third-party copies were out of scope (and if so, provide retention TTL).

• Third-party vendor controls: can Redwood commit to an annual attest report (summary SOC2 or equivalent) for any third-party cold-storage provider used for Aurora data? A redacted controls summary is acceptable.

If we can accept those tightened asks, procurement is willing to proceed to signature after the redlines are incorporated. Otherwise we'll need internal exec review.

Happy to get on a 30m call if helpful.

Best,
Alice
Attachment: (none)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Questions on DPA retention & onshore access (Aurora) — next steps

Alice — thanks. Quick answers and next steps: 

• Notice window: Redwood accepts the 72-hour notice window and will include a short rationale section in the post-incident report describing the legal/regulatory justification.

• Deletion certificate: we will include purge-job identifiers/hashes where technically available and a clear indicator for any archived/third-party copies that are out of scope plus the retention TTL. We will add a short appendix describing snapshot lifecycle semantics so the certificate is interpretable by Aurora's auditors.

• Vendor attest: Redwood will provide an annual redacted controls summary for any third-party cold-storage provider used for Aurora data. If the vendor cannot provide a SOC2, Redwood will provide an internal risk assessment and compensating controls summary.

Action items: Naomi will incorporate Alice's small edits in the DPA redlines doc and send a final redline to Aurora Legal by EOD Monday 2028-04-17. Karthik to coordinate a 30-minute technical walkthrough (snapshot lifecycle + purge job IDs) with Aurora engineering next week. Jordan will add the vendor attest process to the vendor onboarding checklist and share timelines.

We'll attach the redlines and the vendor controls checklist when we send the final. Thanks again for the collaborative approach — happy to move to signature once Aurora confirms.

—Jonas
